subject.name_or_desc: A sick doctor (the patient; the question asked concerning him)

context.question: What was his disease? If curable? What part of the body was afflicted?
context.setting: A decumbiture-type sickness question: the doctor was ill, and Lilly, having little judgment in physic himself, judged from the figure and afterwards spoke with the patient.

attachments.key_positions: The sixth house afflicted by a planet in his fall placed therein; the lord of the Ascendant lately separated from a dexter square of Saturn, Saturn at that time in Cancer (signifying the breast and stomach); the Moon in the fourth house with Saturn; all the angles fixed
attachments.note: Positions as stated in Lilly's prose judgment.

provenance.book: William Lilly, Christian Astrology (1647), Book II
provenance.chapter: Book II, Chap. XLV: a sick doctor — what was his disease, if curable, what part of the body afflicted
